state_of_play.narrative: The diplomatic track lapsed and the long end repriced. The 60-day deadline the US and Iran set in June to reach a final deal expired on 17 August with neither side moving on the Strait of Hormuz or on frozen Iranian funds, and neither willing to extend it; Washington has since turned on Oman, the channel through which the Hormuz-management talks this desk logged on 10 August were running. The IEA now forecasts the widest global oil supply deficit in five years. US stocks fell on it - S&P 500 -0.50% to 7,747, Nasdaq -0.31% to 26,647, Dow -0.51% to 53,460 - but the move that matters was in bonds: the US 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.31%, its highest since 2007, alongside a UK 30-year gilt near 5.77%. Yesterday this desk called the gilt move the first hard transmission of the oil premium; that was too narrow - both G7 long ends went together. It bites harder because the Fed's composition has changed: Chair Kevin Warsh's July meeting held at 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 vote with three regional presidents dissenting in favour of a hike, the most hawkish dissent since 2016, and September is explicitly live. Asia split overnight - Korea +2.2% on memory strength, Japan -1.6% after Q2 GDP grew 1.1% annualised against 2% expected. Gold $4,429 and, after four failed attempts, MSTR pinned from a quoted close at $93.95.

crash_risk.read: The count of flashing clusters is unchanged at the sourced 4 of 7, but the desk's own read is that a fifth channel opened yesterday and it is the one that transmits. The US 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.31% on 17 August, its highest since 2007, on heavy issuance plus tariff and energy inflation - and it did so alongside a UK 30-year gilt near 5.77%. Yesterday this desk described the gilt move as a UK-specific transmission of the oil premium; that was too narrow. The trigger behind it also hardened: the US-Iran 60-day deadline expired on 17 August with no deal and no extension, and the IEA now forecasts the widest global supply deficit in five years. Set against that, the benign 12 Aug CPI (+0.1% m/m) and improved breadth (Russell 2000 record) both still stand, claims at 209k with a 199k four-week average continue to contradict the recession read, and credit spreads are calm. What has changed is the reaction function: Chair Warsh's July FOMC held 9-3 with three dissents in favour of a HIKE, the most since 2016, so a sustained energy premium now runs into a committee already leaning hawkish. Valuation and concentration remain the hot cluster; depth risk ~15-25% on a catalyst; timing un-triggered. The 0-100 composite is the 8 August weekly figure and the weekly re-cut is two appends overdue - do not read it as current.

Power-theme ETFs gathering assets fast
tail: Fluence backlog a record $6.4bn; ~$550m single hyperscaler storage order in July
Google-Kairos-TVA 50 MW Hermes 2 SMR PPA (signed)

The ledger's named leaders, already substantially re-rated - entry here is into strength rather than into a discount.
Grid-scale storage is the leg that ships inside this cycle rather than in 2030 - though Fluence's record $6.4bn backlog is share-taking, not a sector-wide lift.

vehicles: Siemens Energy ENR.DE, Schneider SU.PA, National Grid
access.tradeoff: The European electrical majors are the natural non-US route and are EUR-denominated; National Grid gives regulated sterling exposure but little AI-datacentre torque.

investible_themes.includes: HBM, DRAM and NAND — the memory wall around AI compute.
investible_themes.read: The cleanest recipient in the book and the supply evidence keeps thickening. TrendForce on 13 August put conventional DRAM contract prices at +13-18% q/q and NAND at +10-15%, with HBM4 costing $31-32/GB against HBM3E's $17-18. Samsung's entire 2026 HBM capacity is sold out and its HBM4 yields are reported near 80%. A shortage, not a cycle.
price: leading; HBM order books sold out to 2028
flows: Memory weightings raised across semis funds
Cyclical-recovery inflows into the group
tail: DRAM spot up ~700% y/y; 2026 HBM capacity pre-booked by end-2025
64GB DDR5 RDIMM ~$873 (Q1) to ~$1,586 (Q4 2026), an estimate

access.tradeoff: There is no dedicated memory ETF; broad semi funds hold the memory names at small weights, so a 700% DRAM spot move barely shows through.
The two purest HBM plays are Korean-listed and need international dealing access; the US pair is the practical route for most.
Memory-equipment makers capture the reallocation of capacity to HBM without having to pick between the three DRAM makers.

vehicles: iShares MSCI Korea UCITS, VanEck Semiconductor UCITS
access.tradeoff: A Korea ETF is the practical UK route to Samsung and SK hynix, but it dilutes the memory signal with banks and industrials and is unhedged to KRW.

investible_themes.includes: Transceivers, optical DSPs, co-packaged optics and fibre — the data-movement layer.
investible_themes.read: Confirmed a week ago and holding without a fresh print. Lumentum's FQ4 settled the demand question - $1.01bn revenue, +109% y/y, gross margin through 50%, record 800G and 1.6T production started on plan. The FCC ban is still only drafted, so the reshoring leg remains optional upside rather than the thesis.
flows: Optics allocations rising in Q2 13F filings
Dedicated networking sleeves in AI funds
tail: Record 800G shipments; 1.6T production started, ramping through CY2027
FCC ban still draft; Chinese firms hold >60% of the 800G+ market

access.tradeoff: The nearest wrappers are broad AI-infrastructure and networking funds, in which optics sits at a few percent - there is no clean passive basket for this theme.
The ledger's expression line and the only real way in; valuations are rich (COHR and LITE above 127x trailing) and AAOI is unprofitable.
The substrate and fibre layer is thin because Lumentum and Coherent are vertically integrated - and indium phosphide, which every Western alternative needs, is under Chinese export licensing.
UK investors reach this through US lines in a general dealing account; there is no sterling or UCITS route that isolates optics.

investible_themes.read: A recovery, not a record, and now with a clearer bid. Gold reached $4,429 on 18 August after two straight advances, supported by fading expectations of a Fed hike on soft US data - a read the July FOMC's three hawkish dissents partly contradict. It sits roughly 21% below its 28 January 2026 all-time high near $5,600 after a ~25% correction into June.
flows: Central-bank buying at multi-decade highs
Gold-ETF holdings rising after long outflows
tail: +11.2% off the 14 Jul $4,001 call; Citi $4,500 target stands
Rebuilding from the ~$4,195 June low, not extending a record

access.tradeoff: Tracks bullion with no operating leverage - the cleanest expression of the real-yield thesis itself, and the one that matches the ledger's actual call.
Miners give leverage to the price but add cost inflation, jurisdiction and execution risk that bullion does not carry.
Royalty and streaming names take the price upside without per-ounce cost inflation, at a persistent valuation premium.
These trade in sterling on the LSE and are ISA-eligible, but the underlying is USD gold - sterling strength eats the return even when the metal rises.

investible_themes.includes: Crude and refined products, integrated majors, energy services and tanker tonnage.
investible_themes.read: The negotiated route has lapsed, not merely stalled. The 60-day deadline the US and Iran set in a June memorandum expired on 17 August with neither side moving on the Strait or on frozen funds and neither willing to extend; Iran says the blockade must lift first, and Washington has turned on Oman, the mediating channel. The IEA now forecasts the widest global supply deficit in five years. The premium is priced into both the US and UK long ends, not just the gilt curve as this desk wrote yesterday.
price: Brent $88.31 (17 Aug, sourced); the page's Brent tile is self-flagged unverified at $91.25 and is not the desk's anchor
flows: Energy sector ratings reversed UW to N across the desk's own sector table
Safe-haven bid showing up in gold alongside crude, same driver
tail: US-Iran 60-day deadline expired 17 Aug with no deal and no extension; Hormuz shut on Iran's terms
IEA forecasts the widest global oil supply deficit in five years; UK July CPI lands 19 Aug

access.tradeoff: XLE is equity beta to the premium; USO and BNO track futures, so roll cost means they diverge from spot over any long holding period.
Integrated majors capture the crude move with dividend support, but downstream refining margin partly offsets a spike rather than amplifying it.
Tanker rates rise on rerouting even when volumes fall, which makes tonnage the purest expression of the blockade specifically rather than of the oil price generally.
Shell and BP are sterling LSE lines and the most direct UK route; a Brent ETC gives the commodity without equity risk but carries the same futures roll.

investible_themes.includes: GPU-rental clouds and AI-infra operators renting compute by the hour.
investible_themes.read: The payer layer passed its test - both prints converted capex into contracted, largely pre-paid revenue. What changed this run is the cost of the other side of that trade: with the US 30-year at 5.31%, the highest since 2007, these debt- and prepayment-funded balance sheets face a materially dearer financing stack. Demand is settled; funding is not.
flows: Private credit funding GPU fleets at scale
Sovereign & enterprise pre-commitments rising
tail: CRWV backlog $104bn (+246% y/y), FY26 guide $12.4-13.2bn, capex $35-39bn
NBIS: four contracts >$1bn each, 50-60% of associated capex pre-paid

access.tradeoff: Too new and too small a cohort for a dedicated fund; broad AI-infrastructure ETFs hold CRWV at low single-digit weights.
Contracted, prepaid backlog is what re-rated these; they are debt- and prepayment-funded balance sheets, so financing conditions now matter more than demand.
Owns the shell and the credit rather than the rental margin - lower torque to a neocloud re-rating, and the financiers now sit on both sides of the trade.
The purest remaining neocloud exposure is pre-IPO - Crusoe and Lambda are private, reachable only via secondaries or venture funds, and not accessible to most readers.

investible_themes.includes: Uranium miners, enrichment and small-modular-reactor developers.
investible_themes.read: Term price doing the work and the build is visible. Uranium spot $86.36/lb with the long-term contract around $90, the highest since 2008 and well clear of the sub-$80 invalidation. Fresh dated build evidence this run: construction started at a Saskatchewan uranium mine on 14 August and Spain approved extended operation at Almaraz on 17 August. NuScale reported Q2 on 5 August with liquidity at $1.9bn.
flows: Dedicated nuclear/uranium ETFs gathering assets
Utility & tech PPAs underwriting new capacity
tail: Uranium term price ~$90/lb - highest since 2008; spot ~$84-86
~9.8 GW committed to datacentres, ~80% not yet in commercial operation

access.tradeoff: URA and URNM are uranium-miner heavy and NLR leans utility; none of the three is an SMR pure-play.
Cameco is the producing anchor; Oklo and NuScale are pre-revenue developers whose value sits in 2030-plus offtake, so the two halves behave nothing alike.
HALEU is the binding constraint into 2027-30, which puts the bottleneck in the fuel cycle rather than in reactor design.
Yellow Cake holds physical U3O8 on the LSE in sterling - the cleanest UK route to the term price (~$90/lb, highest since 2008) without mining or construction risk.

investible_themes.read: Structural demand, full multiples, and a dating correction. CrowdStrike and Palo Alto are up roughly 60% and 80% this year and closed at records after Black Hat. This desk had Palo Alto reporting on 18 August; it reports on 1 September. CrowdStrike reports 26 August - the same evening as Nvidia. Threat evidence is live: a CISA/FBI/NSA joint advisory on Gunra ransomware, and an actively exploited Cisco ASA/FTD VPN flaw.
flows: Software funds overweight security platforms
Steady inflows into cyber-theme ETFs
tail: CRWD FY26 rev $4.81bn (+22%); net-new ARR above $1bn for the first time
AI-driven threat volume lifting budgets; CRWD ~90x, PANW ~55x, ZS ~35x forward

access.tradeoff: Broad coverage of a sector whose two leaders are already up 60% and 80% this year - and the funds are top-heavy in exactly those two.
Both leaders sit at record multiples with near-dated prints - CrowdStrike reports 26 August and Palo Alto 1 September (this desk previously had Palo Alto on 18 August; corrected).
The UCITS wrappers are the practical UK route and hold the same US leaders; Europe's own listed pure-plays thinned out after Darktrace was taken private in 2024.

investible_themes.includes: Prime contractors and munitions — US and European primes.
investible_themes.read: The kill-watch recedes. This entry's stated invalidation is a durable Ukraine ceasefire; the 2026 truces were a 32-hour Easter pause in April and a three-day Victory Day pause in May, neither of which held, and the EU agreed a EUR 90bn loan on 23 April for Ukraine's 2026-27 budgetary and defence needs with EUR 4.9bn already disbursed for drones. No European defence budget has been cut. The operating evidence is strong - Rheinmetall Q2 sales +69.8% to EUR 3.289bn, backlog EUR 80.4bn - but H1 free cash flow of -EUR 1.6bn is still the weak leg, and the shares fell 5.7% on it.
flows: Defence & European-defence ETFs seeing steady inflows
UK primes leading on order intake
tail: BAE record GBP84bn backlog; RR raised targets (both carried from July)
New leg: US Navy construction opened to foreign yards with US investment

access.tradeoff: ITA and XAR are US-prime heavy; EUAD is the European-defence wrapper and carries the Ukraine-settlement sensitivity directly.
The ledger's named leaders. Rheinmetall shows the sector's live tension - sales +69.8% and an EUR 80.4bn backlog, sold on -EUR 1.6bn of H1 free cash flow.

vehicles: Hensoldt HAG.DE, Saab SAAB-B.ST, Thales HO.PA,
access.tradeoff: Sensors, electronic warfare and drones sit closer to the parts of the budget that are being re-phased upward, but these are smaller and thinner than the primes.
The UCITS wrappers are the practical UK route and avoid the FX drag of the US funds; both hold the same European primes, so they overlap heavily with a direct BAE or Rolls-Royce line.

investible_themes.includes: Industrial, warehouse and surgical robotics plus automation enablers.
investible_themes.read: Autonomy first, and now with its first regulatory scar. Waymo is past 500,000 paid trips a week and 220 million rider-only miles across 11 cities, is permitted or testing in 26 of the top 30 US metros, and plans 12 more cities in 2026 including London. Against that, NHTSA recorded a June recall of 3,871 fifth-generation driving systems after vehicles entered closed freeway construction zones. Tesla's Optimus Gen 3 still has not been shown.
flows: Automation baskets attracting fresh allocations
Humanoid-robotics venture funding surging
tail: Figure 03 past 1,000 units; AgiBot 15,000 cumulative; ~$4.3bn humanoid funding in 2026
Waymo ~500k paid rides/week across ~10 cities, targeting 1m/week

access.tradeoff: Both leading funds are dominated by legacy factory automation and Japanese industrials - humanoid and robotaxi exposure inside them is close to nil.
Autonomy is the leg with revenue and regulatory approvals, but it arrives inside two megacaps, so the exposure is heavily diluted by everything else they do.
Actuator, sensor and compute suppliers sell to whichever platform wins - but humanoid unit volumes are still measured in thousands, so the revenue is not there yet.
Every humanoid leader is private - roughly $4.3bn went into humanoid startups in 2026 and none of it is reachable on an exchange. This is why the theme reads autonomy-first.
RBOT is the practical UK wrapper, USD-exposed and carrying the same legacy-automation tilt as its US cousins.

investible_themes.includes: Rare-earth miners, processors and magnet makers — inputs to EVs, motors, defence.
investible_themes.read: Better evidenced than a week ago but quiet in August itself. MP's processed rare-earth revenue nearly quadrupled to $94.4m after it stopped sending material to China, with $16.5m from the Texas magnet line. The structural leg firmed in June: the G7 agreed on 17 June to cap rare-earth imports from any single outside source below 60% by 2030, while China still refines around 91% of world output and has blacklisted MP and USA Rare Earth.
price: - USA Rare Earth +9% the same day
flows: Dedicated critical-minerals / rare-earth ETFs launching
Government offtake and price-floor support emerging
tail: Section 232 critical-minerals proclamation live; no duties imposed yet
Ten further minerals pulled into the Section 232 net

access.tradeoff: REMX still carries meaningful Chinese-listed weight, which is awkward for a theme whose entire driver is decoupling from China.
MP and USA Rare Earth are both on China's June 2026 export-control blacklist - the policy that supports the thesis is simultaneously an operating constraint.

vehicles: Magnet and separation capacity: MP's Texas line, Neo Performance NEO.TO, Solvay SOLB.BR
access.tradeoff: Processing and magnets are where the West is shortest, so this is the real bottleneck - but capacity is small and lumpy, which makes revenue volatile.
There is no UCITS rare-earth pure-play; a broad mining trust dilutes the signal heavily, so most UK access is via US and Australian lines directly.

investible_themes.includes: Commercial launch, satellites and payload operators.
investible_themes.read: Deteriorated on timeline, not on demand, and no better this run. Rocket Lab still targets Q4 2026 pad delivery but has not reaffirmed a first flight before year-end, and coverage openly contemplates a 2027 slip - the theme's stated kill condition. The company will run end-to-end performance tests on the pad with the upper stage before installing the Archimedes vacuum engine.

flows: Early space-theme fund launches gathering assets
Defence primes expanding space exposure

ASTS $1.30bn backlog, $2.7bn cash, >60 MNO partners

investible_themes.includes: Bitcoin/ether proxies, exchanges and spot ETFs; stablecoin rails.
investible_themes.read: CORRECTED. This desk wrote yesterday that the CLARITY Act had been shelved with passage likely slipping to 2027. That was over-read: the Senate has scheduled a floor vote for Tuesday 15 September 2026, with cloture already filed on the motion to proceed. The August delay was real and the outstanding disputes - ethics rules, illicit-finance provisions and stablecoin yield - are unresolved, but this is a dated test rather than a dead file.

Corporate treasuries still adding on dips

Coinbase carries US market-structure risk directly, and that risk now has a date on it - the Senate floor vote is set for 15 September; MSTR is a leveraged bitcoin proxy rather than an operating business.
UK retail access to crypto ETNs on recognised exchanges opened in October 2025; these are debt securities, not funds, and the underlying is outside FSCS protection.

Open disputes: government ethics, illicit finance, and stablecoin yield and rewards
signals.assessment: Yesterday this desk wrote that passage was likely slipping to 2027. That was over-read - the delay is real but dated.

signals.headline: CORRECTED: the 401(k) private-assets executive order dates to August 2025, not this month
summary: The executive order was signed 7 August 2025; Blackstone stood up its DC unit in October 2025
The 2026-dated catalyst is the DOL proposal of 30 March 2026, on which the listed alt managers rose
The radar entry's price leg therefore belongs to March, not to August
signals.assessment: An entry promoted yesterday on a year-old catalyst. Held at 4 of 5 and re-dated rather than quietly fixed.

signals.headline: MSTR pinned from a quoted close at $93.95 after four failed attempts
summary: Traded $93.82-$94.48 on 17 August, closing $93.95; market cap $35.76bn
Against the $91.39 call of 14 July the exit flag is +2.8% - leaning wrong
The evening pass had derived ~$93.0 by inverting an analyst target percentage; the derivation was close
signals.assessment: The 'wire a price feed or close the flag' dilemma is resolved: a direct price search works. The flag stays open.

signals.headline: Gold $4,429 on a second straight advance as hike expectations fade
summary: Spot $4,429.49 on 18 August, +0.30% on the day, holding above $4,400
Supported by fading Fed-hike expectations after a string of soft US data
Still roughly 21% below the 28 January all-time high near $5,600
signals.assessment: The bid and the July FOMC's three hawkish dissents point opposite ways. Watch which one the September meeting settles.

signals.headline: CoreWeave Q2: revenue $2.58bn (+112%), backlog $104bn (+246%)
summary: Adjusted loss $1.03/sh vs $1.22 expected; shares rose ~13-14% after hours and ~19% across the post-print stretch
FY26 guidance raised to $12.4-13.2bn with capex of $35-39bn
51 active datacentres, 1.5 GW active power, ~3.7 GW contracted
signals.assessment: The master factor's biggest test, and the payer passed. With the 30Y at 5.31% the financing leg is now the open question.

signals.headline: Nebius Q2: revenue $582m (+454%), adjusted EBITDA positive $236m
summary: EPS -$0.12 against -$0.82 expected; full-year guidance reaffirmed at $3.0-3.4bn
Four core contracts averaging over $1bn each; customer prepayments cover 50-60% of associated capex
Secondary coverage cites $575m and +514% - the company release is the anchor, the divergence is logged not adopted
signals.assessment: Pre-paid, contracted capacity funded by customers rather than by debt alone. Shares rose ~34% post-print.

signals.headline: July CPI benign: +0.1% m/m, 3.4% headline, 2.5% core
summary: Every reading in line with consensus; headline eased from 3.5% and core from 2.6%
No energy pass-through visible yet in the US data
UK July CPI lands 19 August and is expected at a four-month high
signals.assessment: The US print is the reason a hawkish FOMC still held. The UK print tomorrow is where the oil premium shows up first.

signals.headline: Lumentum revenue $1.01bn (+109%) on record 800G, with 1.6T ramping
summary: EPS $3.23 vs $2.97; non-GAAP gross margin crossed 50%
Record 800G cloud transceiver shipments; 1.6T production started on plan
Stock +14.19% on 12 August
signals.assessment: The print that promoted optics to confirmed. No fresh evidence this run - the promotion is one week old and holding.

signals.headline: BIS extends advanced-computing licensing to D:5-parented subsidiaries
summary: Guidance issued 15 August 2026
Licences now required regardless of where the subsidiary itself is located
Closes the third-country routing gap
signals.assessment: Feeds supply-chain security directly and is a second-order tailwind to US-content optics and domestic capacity.

signals.headline: Rheinmetall Q2 sales +69.8%, backlog EUR 80.4bn, but H1 cash flow -EUR 1.6bn
summary: Operating profit +115%; shares fell 5.7% post-print on the cash outflow, then +5.5% on 16 August
Backlog EUR 80.4bn with ~70% firm orders, up from the EUR 64bn this desk had carried
The kill-watch receded this run: the 2026 truces were short and failed, and the EU agreed a EUR 90bn Ukraine loan on 23 April
signals.assessment: Strong orders sold on cash quality. The political driver improved; the cash-conversion question did not.

signals.headline: MP Materials' processed rare-earth revenue nearly quadruples to $94.4m
summary: Achieved after halting shipments of material to China for processing
Texas magnet operations added $16.5m revenue and $7.5m adjusted profit
Structural leg: the G7 agreed on 17 June to cap single-source rare-earth imports below 60% by 2030
signals.assessment: Conversion, not just a price pop. But August itself produced no fresh print - the domain is quiet on a strong base.

signals.headline: Jobless claims 209k with the four-week average unchanged at 199k
summary: Initial claims rose 9,000 in the week to 8 August against a 202,000 median forecast
Continuing claims fell 22,000 to 1.777m; insured unemployment rate steady at 1.2%
The entry named rising continuing claims as its confirmation and got the opposite
signals.assessment: The labour-turn thesis stays stalled. The duration leg now fights a 30-year yield at 5.31% as well.

signals.headline: Rocket Lab: record $2.36bn backlog, but Neutron's first flight stays unreaffirmed
summary: Q4 2026 pad delivery still targeted; the company has not reaffirmed a launch before year-end
End-to-end performance tests will run on the pad with the upper stage before the Archimedes vacuum engine is installed
Coverage openly contemplates a slip into 2027 - the theme's verbatim kill condition
signals.assessment: Unchanged and unimproved for a second run. Demand confirmed, catalyst undated; the theme stays emerging with no access routes.

signals.headline: Cyber date correction: CrowdStrike reports 26 August, Palo Alto 1 September
summary: This desk had Palo Alto reporting 18 August and flagged a 26 Aug vs 2 Sept conflict on CrowdStrike
Company IR settles both: CRWD after the close on 26 August, PANW on 1 September
CRWD and PANW are up roughly 60% and 80% YTD and closed at records after Black Hat
signals.assessment: CrowdStrike now reports the same evening as Nvidia - two record-multiple prints in one session.

signals.headline: US-China tariff truce extended 90 days to 10 November
summary: Executive order signed 11 August, a day ahead of the deadline
The 10% reciprocal tariff on Chinese-origin goods stays in force
The stated kill was a deal that negotiated content tariffs down - the opposite happened
signals.assessment: Kill condition tested and not triggered. The content tariffs survive while talks continue.

signals.headline: Cisco AI infrastructure orders reach $9.3bn for FY26, roughly 4.5x
summary: FQ4 revenue $17.3bn (+18%), non-GAAP EPS $1.22 (+23%), both above guidance
FY27 AI infrastructure revenue targeted at $7.5bn
Stock fell 4.6% after hours on gross-margin guidance
signals.assessment: Demand confirmed, sold on margin mix - the cross-cutting tell that also hit Applied Materials.

signals.headline: Google overhauls DeepMind leadership; Hassabis to chairman, Jeff Dean exits
summary: Announced 5 August; Koray Kavukcuoglu elevated to lead Gemini
Jeff Dean leaving after 27 years
GOOGL fell 4% on the day
signals.assessment: Carried. No further development this run.
